gapFill.title: Fill in the gap
gapFill.subtitle: Type the whole verb phrase — the present simple or the present continuous, whichever the signal word or context calls for. Twenty original sentences.

questions.after: to school by bus every day.
questions.explain: ‘Every day’ is a habit — use the present simple.
‘Be quiet!’ points to something happening right now — use the present continuous.
A scientific fact — use the present simple (with -s for ‘water’).
‘This week’ is a temporary situation — use the present continuous.

questions.after: the answer. Can you help me?
questions.explain: ‘Know’ is a stative verb — it stays in the present simple, even in the negative.
‘Doing’ and ‘at the moment’ show an action in progress — the question takes ‘are’.
‘How often’ asks about a habit — the question takes ‘do’ + base verb.
‘Usually’ shows a routine — use the present simple (with -s for ‘my dad’).
‘Look!’ points to something happening now — use the present continuous.
‘This summer’ is a temporary job — use the present continuous.
‘Like’ is a stative verb — present simple, with -s for ‘Mum’.
A general fact — use the present simple.
‘Listen!’ points to something happening now — use the present continuous.
A permanent situation — the question takes ‘does’ + base verb.
‘On Saturdays’ is a routine — use the present simple.

questions.after: a lot of coffee this month because of the exams.
questions.explain: ‘This month’ is temporary, and it is different from my normal habit — use the present continuous.
‘Belong’ is a stative verb — present simple, with -s for ‘this bag’.
‘At the moment’ — use the present continuous.
‘Laughing’ is an action in progress — the question takes ‘are’.
‘Every twenty minutes’ is a regular pattern — use the present simple.

wordOrder.title: Put the words in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words below to build each sentence in the right order. Twenty original sentences, mixing both tenses.

matching.title: Match the signal word to the tense
matching.subtitle: Tap a signal word or phrase, then tap the tense it points to. Habits and routines take the present simple; actions happening now or temporary situations take the present continuous.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. British English. Ask yourself: is it a habit or fact, or is it happening now? That decides the tense.

questions.text: My mum        to the market every Saturday.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘every Saturday’ is a habit — use the present simple, not the continuous.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘my mum’ use ‘goes’.
Wrong tense: a regular habit takes the present simple, not the present perfect.
questions.explain: ‘Every Saturday’ is a habit — present simple.

questions.text: Shh! The baby        in the next room.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘Shh!’ points to an action happening now — use the present continuous.
Wrong form and tense: ‘Shh!’ points to now, and ‘the baby’ is singular.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘the baby’ is singular — use ‘is’, not ‘are’.
questions.explain: ‘Shh!’ — something is happening right now: present continuous.

questions.text: The Sun        in the east.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: a general fact takes the present simple, not the continuous.
Wrong tense: this is a general fact, not a finished action with a result now — use the present simple.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘the Sun’ is singular — use ‘rises’.
questions.explain: A general fact — present simple.

questions.text: I        at my aunt’s house at the moment because my heating is broken.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘at the moment’ shows a temporary situation in progress — use the present continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘at the moment’ is now, not the past.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘I’ use ‘am’, not ‘are’.
questions.explain: ‘At the moment’ — a temporary situation: present continuous.

questions.text: I        this song — it’s my favourite.
wrongReasons: Wrong form: ‘love’ is a stative verb, so it is not used in the continuous.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘I’ use ‘love’, not ‘loves’.
Wrong tense: ‘it’s my favourite’ is about now, not the past.
questions.explain: ‘Love’ is a stative verb — present simple.

questions.text: We usually        dinner at eight.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘usually’ shows a routine — use the present simple, not the continuous.
Wrong tense: ‘usually’ shows a routine — use the present simple, not the present perfect.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘we’ use ‘have’, not ‘has’.
questions.explain: ‘Usually’ shows a routine — present simple.

questions.text: Look! Those children        in the river!
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘Look!’ points to an action happening now — use the present continuous.
Wrong tense and agreement: ‘Look!’ points to now, and ‘children’ is plural.
Wrong tense: ‘Look!’ shows an action in progress, not a finished one.
questions.explain: ‘Look!’ — an action in progress: present continuous.

questions.text: The shop        at nine o’clock every morning.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘every morning’ is a routine — use the present simple.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘the shop’ is singular — use ‘opens’.
Wrong tense: a routine takes the present simple, not the present perfect.
questions.explain: ‘Every morning’ is a routine — present simple.

questions.text: She        a lot of coffee this week because of her exams.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘this week’ shows a temporary change — use the present continuous.
Wrong tense: this week is not finished, and the sentence is about now, not the past.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘she’ use ‘is’, not ‘are’.
questions.explain: ‘This week’ — a temporary situation: present continuous.

questions.text: What        you doing at the moment?
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: ‘doing’ needs a form of ‘be’, not ‘do’.
Wrong auxiliary: ‘doing’ needs a form of ‘be’, and ‘you’ is not singular.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘you’ use ‘are’, not ‘is’.
questions.explain: ‘Doing’ and ‘at the moment’ — present continuous question with ‘are’.

questions.text: How often        your sister call you?
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: ‘How often’ asks about a habit — use ‘does’ + base verb.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘your sister’ use ‘does’, not ‘do’.
Wrong auxiliary: ‘has’ needs a past participle (‘has called’), and this is a habit.
questions.explain: ‘How often’ asks about a habit — ‘does’ + base verb.

questions.text: Bees        honey.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: this is a general fact — use the present simple.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘bees’ is plural — use ‘make’.
Wrong tense: this is a general fact, not a finished action.
questions.explain: A general fact — present simple.

questions.text: Sorry, I        what you mean.
wrongReasons: Wrong form: ‘understand’ is a stative verb, so it is not used in the continuous.
Wrong form: the negative present simple needs ‘don’t’.
Wrong tense: ‘what you mean’ is about now, not the past.
questions.explain: ‘Understand’ is a stative verb — present simple negative.

questions.text: Hurry up! The taxi        outside.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘Hurry up!’ points to now — use the present continuous.
Wrong form and tense: ‘the taxi’ is singular, and the action is in progress.
Wrong tense: the taxi is waiting now — use the present continuous.
questions.explain: ‘Hurry up!’ — it is happening now: present continuous.

questions.text: The Seine        through Paris.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: this is a permanent fact — use the present simple.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘the Seine’ is singular — use ‘flows’.
Wrong tense: this is a permanent fact, not a finished action.
questions.explain: A permanent fact — present simple.

questions.text: Be careful! You        on my bag.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘Be careful!’ points to now — use the present continuous.
Wrong tense and agreement: this is happening now, and ‘you’ takes no -s.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘you’ use ‘are’, not ‘is’.
questions.explain: ‘Be careful!’ — it is happening now: present continuous.

questions.text: Our train        at ten past six every day.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘every day’ is a regular pattern — use the present simple.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘our train’ is singular — use ‘leaves’.
Wrong tense: a regular pattern takes the present simple.
questions.explain: ‘Every day’ is a regular pattern — present simple.

questions.text: My class        a book about Barcelona this term.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘this term’ shows a temporary activity — use the present continuous.
Wrong form: ‘my class’ is singular, and this term’s activity is in progress.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘my class’ is singular — use ‘is’, not ‘are’.
questions.explain: ‘This term’ — a temporary activity: present continuous.

questions.text: This bag        to my sister, not to me.
wrongReasons: Wrong form: ‘belong’ is a stative verb, so it is not used in the continuous.
Wrong form: ‘belong’ is stative, and ‘this bag’ is singular.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘this bag’ is singular — use ‘belongs’.
questions.explain: ‘Belong’ is a stative verb — present simple.

questions.text: Our dog never        at the postman — he’s too friendly.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘never’ shows a habit — use the present simple.
Wrong tense: ‘he’s too friendly’ is about now, not the past.
Wrong tense and agreement: ‘never’ shows a habit, and ‘our dog’ is singular.
questions.explain: ‘Never’ shows a habit — present simple.

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong. Twenty original sentences.

items.message: A daily habit takes the present simple, not the continuous.
‘Now’ points to an action in progress — use the present continuous.
With ‘my brother’ the present simple verb needs -s.
‘Know’ is a stative verb — it is not used in the continuous.
‘Listen!’ points to something happening now — use the present continuous.
A general fact takes the present simple.
‘At the moment’ shows an action in progress — the question needs ‘are’ + -ing.
‘Right now’ shows an action in progress — use the present continuous.
After ‘doesn’t’ use the base verb, with no -s.
‘Want’ is a stative verb — it is not used in the continuous.
‘Every evening’ is a routine — use the present simple.
‘Now’ shows an action in progress — use the present continuous.
With ‘my mum’ (she) the negative needs ‘doesn’t’.
‘How often’ asks about a habit — the question needs ‘do’ + base verb.
A general fact and a daily pattern take the present simple.
After ‘are’ the verb needs -ing for a temporary situation.
‘Know’ is a stative verb — the question needs ‘do’ + base verb, not ‘are’ + -ing.
‘Every morning’ is a routine — use the present simple.
‘Be quiet!’ points to now — use the present continuous.
‘Belong’ is a stative verb — it is not used in the continuous.

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, signal words, multiple choice, and spot-the-mistake. One pass, then a breakdown of where you’re strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: Our neighbours {{blank}} a barbecue at the moment — it smells great!
items.explain: ‘At the moment’ — use the present continuous.

items.sentText: Maria {{blank}} two languages: Catalan and English.
items.explain: A permanent fact about Maria — present simple, with -s.

items.sentText: I {{blank}} my homework in the library every afternoon.
items.explain: ‘Every afternoon’ is a routine — use the present simple.

items.sentText: Dad {{blank}} a new laptop — he says his old one is too slow.
items.explain: ‘Want’ is a stative verb — present simple, with -s for ‘Dad’.

items.text: Which tense does ‘at the moment’ point to?
wrongReasons: ‘At the moment’ means now — the present simple is for habits and facts.
‘At the moment’ is about now, not the past.
‘At the moment’ is about an action in progress now, not a link from the past.
items.explain: ‘At the moment’ means now — present continuous.

items.text: Which tense does ‘every Sunday’ point to?
wrongReasons: ‘Every Sunday’ is a routine — the continuous is for now or temporary.
‘Every Sunday’ shows a routine, not a link from the past to now.
‘Every Sunday’ is a present routine, not a past action in progress.
items.explain: ‘Every Sunday’ is a routine — present simple.

wrongReasons: ‘Listen!’ points to something happening now — the present simple is for habits.
‘Listen!’ is about now, not a finished past action.
‘Listen!’ points to an action in progress, not a past action with a result now.
items.explain: ‘Listen!’ — something is happening now: present continuous.

items.text: Which tense does ‘on Mondays’ point to?
wrongReasons: ‘On Mondays’ is a routine — the continuous is for now or temporary.
‘On Mondays’ is a present routine, not a past action in progress.
‘On Mondays’ shows a routine, not a link from the past to now.
items.explain: ‘On Mondays’ is a routine — present simple.

items.text: Don’t call her now — she {{blank}} a shower.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘now’ shows an action in progress — use the present continuous.
Wrong form and tense: ‘she’ takes -s, and ‘now’ needs the continuous.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘she’ use ‘is’, not ‘are’.
items.explain: ‘Now’ — an action in progress: present continuous.

items.text: Our school {{blank}} at eight forty-five every day.
wrongReasons: Wrong tense: ‘every day’ is a routine — use the present simple.
Subject-verb agreement: ‘our school’ is singular — use ‘starts’.
Wrong tense: a routine takes the present simple.
items.explain: ‘Every day’ is a routine — present simple.

wrongReasons: Wrong form: ‘believe’ is a stative verb, so it is not used in the continuous.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘I’ use ‘believe’, not ‘believes’.
Wrong tense: this is an opinion now, not a past action with a result.
items.explain: ‘Believe’ is a stative verb — present simple.

items.text: Why {{blank}} you wearing a coat? It’s really hot!
wrongReasons: Wrong auxiliary: ‘wearing’ needs a form of ‘be’, not ‘do’.
Wrong auxiliary: ‘wearing’ needs a form of ‘be’, not ‘does’.
Subject-verb agreement: with ‘you’ use ‘are’, not ‘is’.
items.explain: ‘Wearing’ shows an action in progress — the question needs ‘are’.

items.message: ‘Every evening’ is a routine — use the present simple.
‘Look!’ points to something happening now — use the present continuous.
‘Hate’ is a stative verb — it is not used in the continuous.
With ‘our teacher’ (he/she) the negative needs ‘doesn’t’.
